name: building-903
estimated: the faces the photograph sees, with it as a reference: the clad storeys' windows and frames, the glazed storeys' plinth, piers and mullions, their place behind the forward face (drawn as on the south face), the canopies' depth, and the depth of the roof under the step, drawn with nothing under it; and the faces no photograph shows, drawn as the ones it does
refs_note: the folder of refs/ that holds the reference views (views.json, masks/), which refine, compare, metrics, sky_mask and the viewer's ?sv= read: refs/photos (gitignored), whose views tools/photo_camera.py writes. Its one photograph is taken from the road south-east of the building, about 27 m from its south-east corner, looking north-west and up at the south face and the east end; its camera is fitted to both faces' roof edges against the sky (the south face's at 70.1 m, the east end's low gable from 70.1 m up to its ridge at 70.97 m and down to 69.85 m), to four upright edges and to three corners (the ridge, the east end's north corner and the top of the south face's step forward), held 1.6 m over the LiDAR's ground (1.62 m fitted): a lens of 59.4 degrees across, looking up 15.0 degrees, rms 0.85 px over 46 residuals. Fitted to the edges and uprights alone it wanted a lens of 62.8 degrees and put those three corners 12 to 39 px off: the lines alone do not fix the scale along them

building.title: Building 903 (903), University of Auckland
building.note: outline: building 903's outer ring from the main project's campus.json, in the map's frame; it chooses the crop box and the building's own points (frame.near_outline, measure and topview). The site replaces block 903 by its id.

origin.note: the campus origin, as in campus.json; the landmark's local metres = NZTM (EPSG:2193) minus the NZTM of this point, with grid north

lidar.licence: Auckland Part 1 LiDAR (2024), OpenTopography NZ24_Auckland, doi:10.5069/G9HH6H8T: sourced from LINZ and licensed by Regional Software Holdings Limited for re-use under CC BY 4.0

aerial.licence: Auckland Central 0.06 m Urban Aerial Photos (2023): sourced from LINZ and licensed by Auckland Council for re-use under CC BY 4.0

frame.method: LiDAR building points (class 6) more than min_above m above the ground and within near_outline m of building.outline
frame.thresholds_note: min_above 3.46 m over the door's ground (52.64 m), as 3.0 m over the provisional ground (53.1 m, the median LiDAR ground in the crop box) was: the same returns; the centre from the same points (tower_above), which lie within 1.5 m of the campus map ring taken to local metres. The walls' axis runs along the long faces (bearing -71.7 deg), so z faces south-south-west (bearing 198.3 deg), toward the road along that side. The block's roof runs on to the west past the ring at the same height, and a lower block (about 8 m) stands against its north face

crop_note: 45 m round the outline, so that the crop box takes in the road south and east of the building; the ring is in the map's frame, about 29 m east-north-east of where it stands in local metres here

light.note: estimated: the photograph is taken under a bright overcast, looking north-west at faces that face south-south-west and east-south-east, evenly lit and with no shadow cast. The viewer's sun stands behind the building, to the north (0 deg round, 50 up), weak (1.0, against 8), and its sky's light strong (3.4, against 2.25), at an exposure of 0.78: over the model's screen box the luma (p50) 162 against the photograph's 157, p90 174 against 178 (with the sun at 20 deg and 1.5, at 0.95, 178 and 200; at 0.85, 170 and 182).

ground_note: the LiDAR's ground at the door (step 7, 2026-11-12); the provisional ground was 53.1 m, the median LiDAR ground in the crop box. parts/common.js gives every height as the LiDAR's elevation, and its Y turns it into one over this ground

door.note: before the glazed entrance under the canopy at the south-east corner, as the photograph shows it (the campus map records no entrance or lobby in 903's plans): on the platform 1.1 m out from the glazing, under the canopy (p -36.0, q 16.5 in the building's frame; (36.64, 15.02) in the view frame); steps go down from it to the road, 51.9 to 52.2 m. The LiDAR's ground within 1 m: 11 returns, p10/p50/p90 52.585/52.637/52.652 m
